_meta.indication: XTORO (finafloxacin otic suspension), 0.3% is indicated for the treatment of acute otitis externa (AOE) with or without an otowick, caused by susceptible strains of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus in patients age 1 year and older.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-masked, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group study comparing finafloxacin otic suspension 0.3% versus vehicle
pivotal_trials.population: Patients 6 months of age or older with a clinical diagnosis of AOE of less than 4 weeks duration
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical cure at the Test-of-Cure (TOC) visit in the ITT pathogen positive subset
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical cure at TOC (ITT pathogen positive subset): 71.7% (104/145) finafloxacin vs 33.3% (46/138) vehicle; treatment difference 38.4% (95% CI 27.6%, 49.1%), p < 0.001

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-masked, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group study comparing finafloxacin otic suspension 0.3% versus vehicle
pivotal_trials.population: Patients 6 months of age or older with a clinical diagnosis of AOE of less than 4 weeks duration
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical cure at the Test-of-Cure (TOC) visit in the ITT pathogen positive subset
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical cure at TOC (ITT pathogen positive subset): 68.7% (101/147) finafloxacin vs 40.0% (52/130) vehicle; treatment difference 28.7% (95% CI 17.4%, 40.0%), p < 0.001

key_safety: A total of 618 patients were treated with XTORO in two Phase 3 trials; the most common adverse reactions occurring at an incidence of 1% were ear pruritus and nausea.
target_moa: Finafloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antimicrobial that inhibits the bacterial type II topoisomerase enzymes DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, which are required for bacterial DNA replication, transcription, repair and recombination.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee Meeting was held; no new issues were raised in the review thought to benefit from an Advisory Committee Meeting.

summary.text: NDA 206307 for finafloxacin otic suspension 0.3% (a new molecular entity fluoroquinolone) was received April 25, 2014 and reviewed under Priority review; approval was based on two identically designed Phase 3 vehicle-controlled trials (C-10-018 and C-10-019) and was granted without an advisory committee meeting.

Studies C-10-018 and C-10-019 were two identically designed phase 3 studies.
